title: Philosophy
tagline: From Confucius and Laozi to Zhu Xi, Wang Yangming, Toegye and the Kyoto School
hero_file: Confucius, fresco from a Western Han tomb of Dongping County, Shandong province, China (cropped).jpg
hero_caption: Confucius in a Western Han tomb fresco from Dongping, Shandong, 1st century BC
intro: Philosophy in China, Japan and Korea over two and a half thousand years, from the Hundred Schools of the Warring States to the Kyoto School and New Confucianism. The section follows arguments rather than rituals: how to govern, what human nature is, how mind relates to the world, and what makes a life good. Buddhism and Daoism appear here as bodies of philosophical argument; their practice and institutions belong to the Religion section. Every thinker has a full biography and every key text an introduction, illustrated with manuscripts, early printed editions and portraits from Wikimedia Commons.
